title: Tracing & Cost Debrief — Apr 2–9 2026
content:
Observability — Tracing & Cost Debrief (week Apr 2 — Apr 9, 2026)

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel, Lena Ortiz, Samir Khan, Priya Nair, Riya Mehta (SRE)

Summary:
- This week focused on two correlated issues: a transient cost spike tied to model routing fallbacks and a subtle increase in p95 generation latency across hosted endpoints.
- We ran a short tracing-sample experiment and rolled back when overhead exceeded expectations for high-QPS endpoints.

Key metrics and highlights:
- P95 generation latency (hosted-api/model-gen): 210ms (+18% w/w). Baseline is 178ms.
- Average token cost for public models increased ~12% during Apr 6 spike window (03:10–06:45 UTC).
- Tracing ingestion CPU for collector-group-2 increased by 27% during sample-size=100% window.
- Dashboard refresh lag observed: Grafana panels with >12m query windows returning stale data for up to 3m.

Incident recap (Apr 6, 03:10–06:45 UTC):
- Symptom: sudden rise in per-token egress billed to hosted clusters; product telemetry showed increased model fallback to larger model-variants.
- Root cause hypothesis: cache mis-keys + rollout policy mismatch — prefix cache TTL was zeroed by a recent rollout (PR #1890) so many requests bypassed cache and triggered cold-region routing.
- Mitigation: reverted PR (#1890) to previous keying logic at 04:02 UTC; temporary routing throttle applied to burst pool; cost curve recovered by 06:45 UTC.
- Jira: OBS-421 created for full RCA and long-term fixes.

Tracing changes and experiments:
- Experiment: increased trace sampling for 10% of production synthetic traffic to collect full KV cache traces. Result: collector CPU jump + 14% token latency for sampled requests; data quality was good but overhead unacceptable for 24/7.
- Decision: implement adaptive sampling based on endpoint QPS and latency (low-QPS keep 100% sample for 48h; high-QPS cap at 10% and use probabilistic tail-sampling).
- Follow-up ticket: OBS-433 (adaptive-sampler design doc, owner: Arjun, due 2026-04-16).

Dashboards and telemetry work:
- New dashboard deployed: "cost-by-model-and-region" — quick drilldown by tenant id and model family. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cost-model-region
- Added heatmap panel for KV cache hit ratio across edge clusters (panel id 1422).
- Noted missing annotation for rollout events — dashboard will now surface rollout tags (PR to grafana-dashboards repo: #58).

Action items (owners and dates):
- Maya: complete incident RCA doc and post to confluence (linked_artifacts) — due 2026-04-12.
- Arjun: OBS-433 adaptive sampling design + perf budget (2026-04-16).
- Lena: add rollout annotation to all model dashboards + PR (#58) review (2026-04-13).
- Samir: throttle policy draft for burst pool (COST-87) and test on staging (2026-04-15).
- Priya: add synthetic tests to catch cache TTL regressions and add to CI gating (2026-04-20).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is the cache-keying change a symptom of underlying config drift? need cross-check with release-engineering.
- How to safely measure KV cache hits without adding collector overhead? look into sampling-with-metrics-export instead of full-span export.

Blockers:
- Need RBAC permissions for grafana-dashboards repo from infra-admins to push rollout annotations.
- Staging does not yet replicate production token-cost billing; need billing-mock or synthetic charge generator.

Decisions:
- Rollback PR #1890 (temporary) — will reintroduce after refactor and unit tests around keying logic.
- Adopt adaptive tracing sampling as described above; target pilot by 2026-04-23.

Next sync:
- Quick follow-up standup Tue 2026-04-13 09:30 PT (15 mins) to confirm RCA posted and PRs in flight.

Misc scribbles:
- Slack threads: #ops-cost-spike, #tracing (see thread pins)
- Quick links: /dashboard/cost-by-model, /runbook/cost-anomalies

End of notes.
